finding: Whole decode step in one compiled program
detail: The engine runs each token as one NEFF with the KV cache written on the device and greedy argmax on the device, so the host never waits on a framework per layer. This is most of the 0.6B gain, where the reference spends its time in per-step overhead.

finding: 8B decode sits at the memory-bandwidth floor
detail: At about 23.5 ms per token the 8B engine reads its 16.4 GB of weights at about 95% of one logical NeuronCore's HBM bandwidth (floor about 22.6 ms). The reference runs at about 68%. The 1.5x is real and little headroom is left.

Tensor parallelism and mixture-of-experts were first made to work in lab sessions outside the harness and written into the shared skill. The 14B and 30B-A3B runs then reached 1.75x and 2.65x in their first round.

Every reported number comes from the reviewer rebuilding the engine from source with no cache and timing it on held-out prompts. Held-out scores land within about 4% of the run's own score (8B 1.576 to 1.514, 30B-A3B 2.915 to 2.870).

finding: Lossless speculative decoding helps on real text
detail: Prompt-lookup drafts verified 8 tokens at a time keep greedy outputs and raise real-text generation speed: 5.1-5.4x on 0.6B, 2.45x on 8B, 1.77x on 14B, 2.57x on 30B-A3B, against a reference without speculation.

finding: The agent fixed an accuracy fork
detail: Fable's 0.6B speculative engine lost 6 points on MATH-500 in round 6; by round 9 it matched the reference at the same speed, so the drop was a bug and not a cost of speculation.

Random-token prompts make small models loop, so drafts are easy. Harness scores rose while real-text speed stayed flat: one 0.6B engine went 3.0 to 3.7 in the harness at 2.6-2.8x on real text; 14B went 4.65 to 6.10 at 1.73-1.77x.

finding: Engines that fail on long answers
detail: Two 0.6B speculative engines stopped on long MATH-500 answers with "continuation exceeds the compiled positions". Their harness scores (6.9, 7.2) do not count.

finding: NxD Inference kernel options on Qwen3
detail: The reference's own NKI kernel options fail to compile for Qwen3-8B (QKV width 6,144 above the 4,096 limit), so the reference runs on its compiler-generated path. It is the latest public release, 0.10.18399.
One agent ran pkill -f build_neffs.py and killed another run's harness build; another waited on pgrep -f, which matches its own command line, and never woke. Both became skill rules.
One Opus run compiled kernels through undocumented NKI internals. Its results are excluded everywhere; the skill now requires the documented compile route.

The first pilots computed on the CPU or stayed below 1x. That led to the rule that the executable must link libnrt and run on the NeuronCores, and to excluding target/ from snapshots after a cached build leaked into a "clean" rebuild.
